label: early-prefix combination detector (h/2 then f/j), positions 3-5
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). About 80% of its mass falls in the original phase at t=3-5 and it never fires at t<3. It is strongly enriched for particular earlier tokens: first token h or 2 (lift about 9x), with f, j, u or p at positions 1-2 and v or u just before. The strongest examples are prefixes like 2 j f v v and h f j v e. It looks like a hash-like conjunction of the first few tokens, not a clean rule. Simple predicates top out at dev F1 0.12: precision is 0.35 at about 7% recall, and widening the token sets raises recall to about 0.36 but drops precision to about 4%. Sequences with the same prefix tokens often do not fire, and it also fires on many other prefixes (r f p t v, j u f w). About 20% of its mass is in the delimiter and copy phases, at recall_idx 3-5. Magnitude is highest for the h/2 + f/j prefixes at t=3-4; no monotonic modulator was found.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+7.41), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+7.33), out_tok=r (+4.52), out_tok=h (+4.39), orig0=h (+4.18), orig0=2 (+3.92). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-5.04), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.26), recall_idx=1 (-3.26), prev_tok=h (-2.74).
